scenes.text: Just reading about yawning can make you yawn.
About half of adults yawn after seeing someone else do it.
In one Duke study, two hundred twenty two out of three hundred twenty eight people caught at least one.
Some studies found yawns spread most between family, then friends, then strangers.
But other studies couldn't repeat that link to empathy, so scientists still debate it.
Most children don't catch yawns until they're around four years old.
Chimpanzees and dogs can catch yawns too, sometimes just from hearing one.
In a twenty seventeen study at the University of Nottingham, volunteers watched videos of people yawning.
Some were told not to yawn, but they yawned just as often.
People with a more excitable motor area in the brain tended to yawn more.
So why do we yawn at all? One leading idea is that it helps cool the brain.
In one study, people yawned more when it was about twenty degrees Celsius outside.
Yawning even begins before birth, in the womb.
Still, nobody knows for sure why yawns are so contagious.
Did you yawn while watching this? Be honest in the comments.

title: Did you just yawn? Here's why 🥱
caption: About half of adults catch a yawn just by seeing one, and even reading about it can trigger it. Scientists still don't fully agree on why.
